instructions: The night before, or at least 4 hours ahead: pound the chicken breasts to an even 1/2 inch thickness. Put them in a zip-top bag with 1 cup of the buttermilk, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/2 tsp of the pepper. Seal, turn to coat, and refrigerate.
Heat the oven to 250°F. Set a baking sheet with a rack in it for keeping the chicken warm.

Make the waffle batter first so it can sit. Whisk 1 cup of the cornmeal, 1 cup of the flour, the baking powder, baking soda and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl. Whisk 2 cups of the buttermilk, the eggs, melted butter and 1/4 cup of the maple syrup in a smaller bowl. Stir the wet into the dry until just combined. Slice the scallions and mince the chives, then fold them into the batter with the cheddar.

Mix the remaining 1 1/4 cups flour, the remaining 1/2 cup cornmeal, the paprika, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper in a shallow dish. Pour the remaining 1 cup buttermilk into a second shallow dish.
Lift the chicken out of the bag and pat it dry. Slice each breast into strips about 1 inch wide.

Pour the oil into a heavy skillet or Dutch oven to about 1 inch deep and heat over medium-high heat to 350 to 375°F. No thermometer? A pinch of the flour mixture should sizzle right away when it hits the oil. Put the waffle iron on to heat.
Coat each strip in the flour mixture, dip it in the buttermilk, then coat it in the flour mixture again. Shake off the extra.

Lower 3 or 4 strips into the oil. Stand back a little. They'll spatter. Fry for 6 to 8 minutes, turning with tongs, until deep golden and crisp. Cut one open to check: it's done when there's no pink left. Don't crowd the pan.
Transfer the strips to the rack on the baking sheet and keep them warm in the oven. Taste the first strip. If it's flat, sprinkle the rest with a pinch more salt as they come out of the oil.
Fry the rest of the chicken in batches, letting the oil come back up to temperature between them.
Cook the waffles in the greased, hot iron for 5 to 7 minutes each, until browned and crisp. Keep the finished ones warm in the oven with the chicken.
Stack 2 waffles on each plate, top with chicken strips and drizzle with the remaining 1/2 cup maple syrup. Put the hot sauce on the table for the adults.
advance_prep_notes: brine the chicken at least 4 hours ahead or overnight
method_notes: Lead is Garlic and Zest (4.1 from 74): buttermilk-brined chicken strips, dredged in flour and cornmeal and fried, with cornmeal cheddar waffles, scallions and chives. Food Network's sheet-pan version (cornflake chicken on frozen waffles) had no readable rating. The base is kept mild: the lead's 2 tbsp hot sauce in the brine and pinch of cayenne in the coating are left out, and hot sauce goes on the table instead. Scaled to 3 breasts for 4 people. It needs a waffle iron, and the written time is about 65 minutes plus the brine.
